questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place where I could have a certain economic freedom and where I could get in with my grades

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You get most things served on a silver palte for you and its very easy to find information if needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got mails, there were presentations and I always had people to ask about problems. The Erasmus office was always helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I didn't choose the place (Hostivar), I just got placed there with the rest of the faculty of arts

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen was pretty bad with only a sink and a stove. We didn't have oven

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its the best experience ever. The accommodation might be lackluster, but due to all the people you meet, you won't think too much about it and you'll fall in love with it in the end and have the best experience. Just make sure to go to the common room when there's a party. That's the easiest way of making friends

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just showed up at registration day, found the room, filled a piece of paper, and that was it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office was the main help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I overslept on the day of the registration, but there's so many interesting courses that you won't be missing the ones you didn't get to start with

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk with people at registration and make some friends. They're all looking for friends just like you, and something so simple as a conversation with them can ease your own, and their mind if feeling stressed about making friends

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A little bit easy. I was so lucky to have few courses where we got homework so I had a lot of spare time to hang out with friends and go on trips around the country and the surrounding countries. But if I had problems, the teachers would hold office hours every week to settle doubts

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Its very much the same with just the teacher speaking for the duration of the class with minimal student interaction.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Colonial propaganda in cinematography, Medieval Psychology and Empirical Science, Ancient Mysteries and the Environment: Religion and Mythology of Sacred Nature, Milestones of Older Czech History (until 19th Century), The Czechs in the Austrian Monarchy 1740 - 1848, History, Art and Archaeology of Cyprus: from the Neolithic to the Roman province

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Milestones of older czech history, because its 8 credits and there's no homework you need to do from week to week. Its just once a week where the teacher talks without stopping and that's it. Make sure to take notes tho

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: none that I can think of. Everything was a third the price of Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer was very cheap, as well as entrance to night clubs. Trains were also incredibly cheap. Flixbus to Vienna was more expensive than I thought it would be, but the best means of transportation when going to neighboring countries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered sports courses, and with my friends we played volleyball every friday in courts we could rent, as well as occasionally playing football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to parties and esn sporting and travel events. Its cheap and makes it easy to make friends or bond with you friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to the czech towns as they have some very beautiful towns, as well as going to neighboring countries as everything is pretty close by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't talk with a single czech student

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People can be surprisingly racist. Multiple times I had to almost get into fights with or push away drunk people because they were abusing my indian friend

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the beer culture made beer incredibly cheap

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take initiative and don't be afraid of making friends. Everyone is in the same situation as you and don't know anyone. Go to the social events and travel since you have more spare time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: none that I can think about that I advent mentioned

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being so close to your friends. Since most of my friends lived at the same dorm, I was always only 5 minutes away, if not less, from all of my friends whom I would see on a daily basis

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping in contact with your friends from back at home. I kept forgetting about them as it felt like I was living another life, and I was always so busy with my friends in Prague that I completely forgot about my friends back at home. Another challenge could also be getting used to the new place and so many new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
